subject: Temporary hold request for debug logs — ACME integration
messages:
From: samir@acme.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Strange tokenization errors during live run — need a short hold on logs

Hi Alex —

We saw a regression in our integration tests last night that only shows up in production traffic. Support asked us to pull logs and a few request payloads so they can reproduce the failure; engineering needs the full trace for ~48 hours to debug. Are you able to put a short, scoped hold on deletion for the following session IDs? I attached a small manifest with the session IDs and representative timestamps.

- Session window: 2027-04-11T22:30 - 2027-04-12T02:00 UTC
- Session IDs: see acme_debug_manifest.csv (attached)

We know Redwood’s default retention is in effect; this is a time-limited request to help us root cause a customer-impacting issue. If you need an internal request form or approvals, tell me what you need and we’ll get it over quickly.

Thanks,
Samir Kapoor
Platform Engineer, ACME Corp

Attachments: acme_debug_manifest.csv (csv)
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Strange tokenization errors during live run — need a short hold on logs

Folks — forwarding an external request from ACME. They want a very narrow, timeboxed hold so their SREs can reproduce a regression. Quick ask: what’s the minimal approval path for a 48-hour, session-scoped hold and what controls/artefacts do we need to produce?

My thoughts:
- Record the approval in a Jira SUP ticket (I started SUP-2345)
- Export only the listed session IDs to a secure bucket (KMS-protected) rather than extending global retention
- Timebox the hold to 48 hours and log the action in the audit trail

I’m happy to pull together the retention_exception_form.pdf if legal/security want it.

— Alex
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Strange tokenization errors during live run — need a short hold on logs

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. From a CS/legal perspective we need:
1) explicit customer consent in writing for the specific session IDs (Samir’s mail is OK but ask for a one-line confirmation that they approve Redwood to pull/retain those sessions for debugging)
2) the exact scope (session IDs + timestamps) and retention window (48 hours) documented in SUP-2345
3) that the export is a copy to a customer-limited S3 path with KMS using a Redwood key; no changes to production retention settings

If ACME signs off on those three items, I’m comfortable routing approval to security for a time-limited exception. I can draft the one-line confirmation request to Samir if you want.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, alex_martinez@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Strange tokenization errors during live run — need a short hold on logs

Thanks — looping in security review. Conditions for approval:
- Scope: only the session IDs listed in acme_debug_manifest.csv. No broad retention changes.
- Duration: max 48 hours from the time the export completes.
- Export must be to a read-restricted, KMS-encrypted bucket with access granted to a named ACME principal and Redwood SRE group for debugging.
- All actions (export, grant, revoke) must be recorded in the audit log and linked to SUP-2345.
- We require the customer to sign the retention_exception_form.pdf or send a one-line email explicitly authorizing the hold.

If those are met I approve. I’ll note this in the internal compliance tracker and add the approval stamp for SUP-2345. One operational note: ops will perform the export and then immediately revoke external access after the 48-hour window; they should not change cluster-level retention settings.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Security & Compliance
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Samir — thanks for the quick response earlier. Quick update and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

1) What we need from ACME: please reply to this thread with a one-line confirmation that you authorize Redwood to export and retain copies of the session IDs listed in acme_debug_manifest.csv for 48 hours strictly for debugging. That will satisfy legal.

2) What Redwood will do (approved):
   - Create Jira ticket SUP-2345 and attach the manifest and retention_exception_form.pdf
   - Export only the sessions in the manifest to a KMS-encrypted bucket (read access for one named ACME principal)
   - Timebox access for 48 hours from export completion and revoke automatically; all steps logged in the audit trail

3) Operational links/IDs: SUP-2345: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-2345 — Ops will post the bucket path there.

Please reply with the one-line confirmation and we’ll kick off the export immediately.
